    "# Inspect top skills in reskill_optimal\n",
    "# Attention: hard-coded for one scenario at a time [at_risk, shortage]\n",
    "\n",
    "import os\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "\n",
    "# 1) Load the aggregated simulation output\n",
    "base = os.path.join(\n",
    "    useful_paths.figure_dir,\n",
    "    \"reskilling_simulation\",\n",
    "    \"reskill-optimal_wage-opt_regC_2023\",\n",
    ")\n",
    "sim = pd.read_pickle(os.path.join(base, \"reskill-optimal_wage-opt_regC_2023.pkl\"))\n",
    "\n",
    "# 2) Pull out the “job pool”\n",
    "df_cells = pd.concat(sim[\"at_risk\"].values(), axis=0)\n",
    "\n",
    "# 3) Identify all added‐skill‐label columns\n",
    "skill_cols = [c for c in df_cells.columns if c.startswith(\"added_skill_label_step_\")]\n",
    "\n",
    "# 4) Melt into long form: one row per (cell, step, skill_label)\n",
    "df_long = (\n",
    "    df_cells\n",
    "    .reset_index()[[\"orig_ISCO08_3D\"] + skill_cols]\n",
    "    .melt(\n",
    "        id_vars=\"orig_ISCO08_3D\",\n",
    "        value_vars=skill_cols,\n",
    "        var_name=\"step\",\n",
    "        value_name=\"skill_label\"\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    .dropna(subset=[\"skill_label\"])\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# 5) Aggregate counts\n",
    "agg = (\n",
    "    df_long\n",
    "    .groupby(\"skill_label\")\n",
    "    .agg(\n",
    "        total_cells=(\"skill_label\", \"size\"),              # how many cells received that skill\n",
    "        unique_orig_ISCO=(\"orig_ISCO08_3D\", \"nunique\")    # in how many source occupations\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    .reset_index()\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# 6) Rank and pick top 10\n",
    "agg[\"rank\"] = agg[\"total_cells\"].rank(method=\"first\", ascending=False)\n",
    "top10 = agg.sort_values(\"rank\").head(30)[[\"rank\", \"skill_label\", \"total_cells\", \"unique_orig_ISCO\"]]\n",
    "\n",
    "# 7) Show results\n",
    "print(top10.to_string(index=False))\n",
    "\n",
    "# 8) Save to CSV\n",
    "os.makedirs(useful_paths.table_dir, exist_ok=True)\n",
    "csv_path = os.path.join(useful_paths.table_dir, \"top10_added_skills_optimal_at_risk.csv\")\n",
    "top10.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)\n",
    "print(f\"\\nTop 30 skills saved to {csv_path}\")"

   "source": [
    "# Inspect example transitions in reskill_optimal\n",
    "\n",
    "# 1) Load the simulation output\n",
    "base = os.path.join(\n",
    "    useful_paths.figure_dir,\n",
    "    \"reskilling_simulation\",\n",
    "    \"reskill-optimal_wage-opt_regC_2023\",\n",
    ")\n",
    "sim_results = pd.read_pickle(os.path.join(base, \"reskill-optimal_wage-opt_regC_2023.pkl\"))\n",
    "\n",
    "# 2) Pull out the “job pool” → “XX” table\n",
    "df_de = sim_results[\"at_risk\"][\"RO\"]\n",
    "\n",
    "# 3) Drop national-level rows (NUTS_ID ending in \"00\")\n",
    "mask = ~df_de.index.get_level_values(\"NUTS_ID\").str.endswith(\"00\")\n",
    "df_de = df_de.loc[mask]\n",
    "\n",
    "# 4) Pick a cell by index (e.g. position 3)\n",
    "key = df_de.index[3]                # change 3 to any valid row\n",
    "countryw, nuts_id, nace2 = key\n",
    "row = df_de.loc[key]\n",
    "\n",
    "# 5) Build journey table for steps 1–5 (plus original/target labels)\n",
    "cols = [\"orig_ISCO08_3D_label\"]\n",
    "for step in range(1, 6):\n",
    "    cols += [\n",
    "        f\"added_skill_label_step_{step}\",\n",
    "        f\"n_viable_transitions_step_{step}\",\n",
    "        f\"earnings_delta_closest_switch_step_{step}\",\n",
    "        f\"transition_target_step_{step}\",\n",
    "    ]\n",
    "journey = row[cols].to_frame(name=\"value\").reset_index().rename(columns={\"index\": \"metric\"})\n",
    "\n",
    "# 6) Find the first step unlocking a viable transition\n",
    "nv = journey[journey.metric.str.startswith(\"n_viable_transitions\")].copy()\n",
    "nv[\"step\"] = nv.metric.str.extract(r\"step_(\\d+)\").astype(int)\n",
    "first_ok = int(nv[nv.value.astype(float) >= 1].step.iloc[0])\n",
    "\n",
    "# 7) Prepare for plotting\n",
    "nv_plot = nv[nv.step <= first_ok].copy()\n",
    "nv_plot[\"value\"] = nv_plot.value.astype(float)\n",
    "\n",
    "# 8) Plot\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))\n",
    "\n",
    "# a) transitions curve\n",
    "ax.plot(nv_plot.step, nv_plot.value, marker=\"o\", linewidth=2)\n",
    "\n",
    "# b) unlock point\n",
    "unlock_val = nv_plot.loc[nv_plot.step == first_ok, \"value\"].iloc[0]\n",
    "ax.scatter([first_ok], [unlock_val], color=\"red\", zorder=5)\n",
    "\n",
    "# c) dashed lines at y=1 and y=2\n",
    "ax.axhline(1, linestyle=\"--\", linewidth=1)\n",
    "ax.axhline(2, linestyle=\"--\", linewidth=1)\n",
    "\n",
    "# d) title with orig → target\n",
    "orig_label = journey.loc[journey.metric==\"orig_ISCO08_3D_label\", \"value\"].iloc[0]\n",
    "tgt_label = journey.loc[journey.metric==f\"transition_target_step_{first_ok}\", \"value\"].iloc[0]\n",
    "ax.set_title(f\"{orig_label} → {tgt_label}\\n(unlocked at step {first_ok})\", pad=20, fontsize=10)\n",
    "\n",
    "# e) annotate earnings in the middle of plot\n",
    "earn = float(journey.loc[\n",
    "    journey.metric==f\"earnings_delta_closest_switch_step_{first_ok}\", \"value\"\n",
    "])\n",
    "ax.text(\n",
    "    first_ok, unlock_val * 0.7,\n",
    "    f\"Δ earnings: €{earn:.2f}\",\n",
    "    ha=\"center\", fontsize=9,\n",
    "    bbox=dict(boxstyle=\"round,pad=0.3\", alpha=0.2)\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# f) added-skill labels below x-ticks\n",
    "for s in range(1, first_ok + 1):\n",
    "    skill = journey.loc[journey.metric==f\"added_skill_label_step_{s}\", \"value\"].iloc[0]\n",
    "    ax.text(s, -0.2, skill, rotation=45, ha=\"right\", va=\"top\", fontsize=7)\n",
    "\n",
    "# styling\n",
    "ax.set_xticks(range(1, first_ok + 1))\n",
    "ax.set_yticks([0, 1, 2])\n",
    "ax.set_ylim(0, nv_plot.value.max() + 0.5)\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel(\"\", fontsize=9, labelpad=30)\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Viable transitions\", fontsize=9)\n",
    "ax.tick_params(axis=\"both\", labelsize=8)\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "\n",
    "# 9) Save outputs\n",
    "# Ensure table directory exists\n",
    "table_dir = useful_paths.table_dir\n",
    "os.makedirs(table_dir, exist_ok=True)\n",
    "csv_path = os.path.join(table_dir, f\"journey_{countryw}_{nuts_id}_{nace2}.csv\")\n",
    "# save only up to unlock step\n",
    "journey[journey.metric.str.contains(\"orig|step\")].loc[:first_ok].to_csv(csv_path, index=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "out_path = os.path.join(\n",
    "    useful_paths.figure_dir,\n",
    "    f\"journey_plot_{countryw}_{nuts_id}_{nace2}.png\"\n",
    ")\n",
    "# then save with bbox_inches and dpi as keywords on savefig\n",
    "fig.savefig(out_path, bbox_inches=\"tight\", dpi=300)"

    "# Collect raw model output across all options (reg/no-reg) and scenarios\n",
    "# -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",

    "# names and paths\n",

    "# old name: \"reskilling_final_thresh-viable-isco4d-v2\"\n",
    "fmt_string = \"{reskilling_mode}_wage-opt_{regional_constraint}_{year}\"\n",
    "output_dir = os.path.join(useful_paths.data_processed, \"eulfs\", \"reskilling_model_results\")\n",
    "fname = \"model_data_tidy_{}_{}\".format(year, threshold) # add _new once model reran\n",
    "\n",
    "if overwrite_model_results:\n",
    "    # iterate across all options\n",
    "    data_store = {}\n",
    "\n",
    "    for reskilling_mode in reskilling_modes:\n",
    "        for regional_constraint in regional_constraints:\n",
    "            fpath = os.path.join(\n",
    "                useful_paths.figure_dir,\n",
    "                #\"test\",  # todo: delete after testing\n",
    "                folder_name.format(threshold=threshold),\n",
    "                fmt_string.format(\n",
    "                    reskilling_mode=reskilling_mode,\n",
    "                    regional_constraint=regional_constraint,\n",
    "                    year=year\n",
    "                ),\n",
    "                \"{}.pkl\".format(\n",
    "                    fmt_string.format(\n",
    "                        reskilling_mode=reskilling_mode,\n",
    "                        regional_constraint=regional_constraint,\n",
    "                        year=year\n",
    "                    )\n",
    "                ),\n",
    "            )\n",
    "            data_store[\n",
    "                (threshold, reskilling_mode, regional_constraint)\n",
    "            ] = pd.read_pickle(fpath)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # save to pickle\n",
    "    fdir_out = os.path.join(\n",
    "        useful_paths.figure_dir,\n",
    "        #\"test\",\n",
    "        folder_name.format(threshold=threshold),\n",
    "        \"model_data_store.pkl\"\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "    with open(fdir_out, \"wb\") as handle:\n",
    "        pickle.dump(data_store, handle, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "    # Build up aggregated data cube of modelling results across all scenarios\n",
    "    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "    data_tidy = []\n",
    "    for model_version in tqdm(list(data_store.keys())):\n",
    "        # threshold - reskilling - regional constraint\n",
    "        sub_dict = data_store[model_version]\n",
    "\n",
    "        for job_pool in job_pools:\n",
    "            # pool - country - DATA\n",
    "            df_pool = pd.concat(list(sub_dict[job_pool].values()))\n",
    "\n",
    "            # only keep select variables\n",
    "            df_pool_sel = df_pool\n",
    "\n",
    "            # add metadata of model run\n",
    "            df_pool_sel = df_pool_sel.assign(\n",
    "                job_pool=job_pool,\n",
    "                viability_threshold=model_version[0],\n",
    "                reskilling_mode=model_version[1],\n",
    "                regional_constraint=model_version[2]\n",
    "            )\n",
    "\n",
    "            # append\n",
    "            data_tidy.append(df_pool_sel)\n",
    "\n",
    "    df_tidy = pd.concat(data_tidy)\n",
    "    df_tidy = df_tidy.reset_index()\n",
    "\n",
    "    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "    # Clean data set\n",
    "    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "    # rename job pools\n",
    "    df_tidy = df_tidy.replace(scenario_mapping)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # make sure entries for countries with missing earnings data_transitions are coded as NaNs\n",
    "    #earnings_data_missing = [\"AT\", \"ES\", \"CZ\", \"NO\", \"SE\", \"GR\", \"IS\", \"UK\"] #old\n",
    "    earnings_data_missing = ['IT', 'NL', 'DE', 'HU', 'AT', 'RO', 'PL', 'ES', 'LT', 'CY', 'BE', 'CZ', 'HR', 'IS', 'LV']\n",
    "    df_tidy.loc[\n",
    "        df_tidy[\"COUNTRYW\"].isin(earnings_data_missing),\n",
    "        \"earnings_delta_closest_switch_sum_mio\",\n",
    "    ] = np.nan\n",
    "\n",
    "    # add nace labels\n",
    "    df_tidy = pd.merge(df_tidy, rp.nace_labels, on=\"NACE2_1D\", how=\"left\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Save concatenated results data\n",
    "    utils.save_df_to_files(\n",
    "        df=df_tidy,\n",
    "        output_dir=output_dir,\n",
    "        fname_no_ext=fname\n",
    "    )\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    # read results from existing model run\n",
    "    df_tidy = pd.read_pickle(os.path.join(output_dir, fname + \".pkl\"))"

    "#OLD\n",
    "\n",
    "# define columns to be melted\n",
    "transitions_cols = df_tidy.columns[df_tidy.columns.str.startswith(\"n_viable_transitions\")].values\n",
    "viability_cols = df_tidy.columns[df_tidy.columns.str.startswith(\"n_viable_transitions\")].values\n",
    "\n",
    "# per observation\n",
    "earnings_cols = df_tidy.columns[df_tidy.columns.str.startswith(\"earnings_delta_closest_switch_sum_step\")].values\n",
    "index_cols = set(df_tidy.columns) - set(transitions_cols) - set(earnings_cols)\n",
    "\n",
    "# per worker\n",
    "earnings_cols_rel = df_tidy.columns[df_tidy.columns.str.startswith(\"earnings_delta_closest_switch_step\")].values\n",
    "index_cols_rel = set(df_tidy.columns) - set(transitions_cols) - set(earnings_cols_rel)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Re-mask income data for countries that don’t report data (!)\n",
    "df_tidy.loc[df_tidy[\"COUNTRYW\"].isin(iso_missing_earnings), earnings_cols] = np.nan\n",
    "df_tidy.loc[df_tidy[\"COUNTRYW\"].isin(iso_missing_earnings), earnings_cols_rel] = np.nan\n",
    "\n",
    "# Define mapping from job_pool to appropriate norm_factor column\n",
    "norm_factors_by_pool = {\n",
    "    \"at_risk\": \"COEFFY_share_unviable_to_decarbonize\",\n",
    "    \"AR\": \"COEFFY_share_unviable_to_decarbonize\",\n",
    "    \"shortage\": \"COEFFY_share_shortage\",\n",
    "    \"SH\": \"COEFFY_share_shortage\",\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "# Normalize each row using the correct job_pool-specific factor\n",
    "for col in earnings_cols_rel:\n",
    "    df_tidy[col] = df_tidy.apply(\n",
    "        lambda row: row[col] / row[norm_factors_by_pool[row[\"job_pool\"]]]\n",
    "        if norm_factors_by_pool.get(row[\"job_pool\"]) in row\n",
    "        and pd.notna(row[col])\n",
    "        and row[norm_factors_by_pool[row[\"job_pool\"]]] > 0\n",
    "        else np.nan,\n",
    "        axis=1\n",
    "    )\n",
    "df_tidy[[col for col in earnings_cols_rel] + [\"job_pool\"]].groupby(\"job_pool\").describe()\n",
    "\n",
    "# melt to long format\n",
    "df_tidy_long_transitions = df_tidy.melt(id_vars=index_cols, value_vars=transitions_cols, var_name=\"reskilling_step\", value_name=\"n_transitions\")\n",
    "df_tidy_long_transitions[\"reskilling_step\"] = df_tidy_long_transitions[\"reskilling_step\"].str.split(\"_\").str[-1].astype(int)\n",
    "\n",
    "# absolute earnings losses (per-observation numbers)\n",
    "df_tidy_long_earnings_abs = df_tidy.melt(id_vars=index_cols, value_vars=earnings_cols, var_name=\"reskilling_step\", value_name=\"earnings_delta_abs\")\n",
    "df_tidy_long_earnings_abs[\"reskilling_step\"] = df_tidy_long_earnings_abs[\"reskilling_step\"].str.split(\"_\").str[-1].astype(int)\n",
    "\n",
    "# relative earnings losses (per-worker numbers)\n",
    "df_tidy_long_earnings_rel = df_tidy.melt(id_vars=index_cols_rel, value_vars=earnings_cols_rel, var_name=\"reskilling_step\", value_name=\"earnings_delta_rel\")\n",
    "df_tidy_long_earnings_rel[\"reskilling_step\"] = df_tidy_long_earnings_rel[\"reskilling_step\"].str.split(\"_\").str[-1].astype(int)\n",

    "# other earnings figures\n",
    "df_tidy_long_earnings_abs[\"earnings_delta_abs_mio\"] = df_tidy_long_earnings_abs[\"earnings_delta_abs\"] / 10 ** 6\n",

   "source": [
    "\n",
    "- [https://seaborn.pydata.org/tutorial/error_bars.html](https://seaborn.pydata.org/tutorial/error_bars.html), [https://acclab.github.io/bootstrap-confidence-intervals.html](https://acclab.github.io/bootstrap-confidence-intervals.html)\n",
    "- The confidence interval is constructed by taking a percentile interval of the bootstrap distribution**. By default errorbar=\"ci\" draws a 95% confidence interval.\n",
    "- The nonparametric approach to representing uncertainty uses bootstrapping: a procedure where the dataset is randomly resampled with replacement a number of times, and the estimate is recalculated from each resample. This procedure creates a distribution of statistics approximating the distribution of values that you could have gotten for your estimate if you had a different sample. The nonparametric bootstrap has advantages similar to those of the percentile interval: it will naturally adapt to skewed and bounded data in a way that a standard error interval cannot. It is also more general. While the standard error formula is specific to the mean, error bars can be computed using the bootstrap for any estimator\n",
    "- Percentile intervals also represent the range where some amount of the data fall, but they do so by computing those percentiles directly from the sample. By default, errorbar=\"pi\" will show a 95% interval, ranging from the 2.5 to the 97.5 percentiles. You can choose a different range by passing a size parameter, e.g., to show the inter-quartile range."
   ]

    "- levels: int or vector\n",
    "- Number of contour levels or values to draw contours at. A vector argument must have increasing values in [0, 1]. Levels correspond to iso-proportions of the density: e.g., 20% of the probability mass will lie below the contour drawn for 0.2. Only relevant with bivariate data.\n",
    "- thresh: number in [0, 1]\n",
    "- Lowest iso-proportion level at which to draw a contour line. Ignored when levels is a vector. Only relevant with bivariate data.\n"

    "kind = \"bar\"\n",
    "palette = \"BrBG_r\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# make country-level grouped stripplot\n",
    "aggdict = {\n",
    "    \"n_viable_transitions\": np.mean,\n",
    "    \"earnings_delta_closest_switch_sum_mio\": np.mean,\n",
    "    \"viability_threshold\": \"first\",\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "df = df_regions.loc[\n",
    "    (df_regions[\"reskilling_mode\"].isin([\"baseline\", \"reskill-tailored\"]))\n",
    "    & (df_regions[\"regional_constraint\"] == \"regC\")\n",
    "]\n",
    "order = (\n",
    "    df.loc[\n",
    "        (\n",
    "            df_regions[\"reskilling_mode\"].isin([\"baseline\"])\n",
    "            & (df_regions[\"job_pool\"] == \"CPO\")\n",
    "        )\n",
    "    ]\n",
    "    .groupby(\"COUNTRYW\")\n",
    "    .agg(aggdict)\n",
    "    .reset_index()\n",
    "    .sort_values(x, ascending=False)\n",
    "    .loc[:, \"COUNTRYW\"]\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# boxplots\n",
    "g = sns.catplot(\n",
    "    data=df,\n",
    "    col=col,\n",
    "    x=x,\n",
    "    y=y,\n",
    "    hue=hue,\n",
    "    order=order,\n",
    "    col_order=col_order,\n",
    "    hue_order=hue_order_main,\n",
    "    kind=kind,\n",
    "    sharey=sharey,\n",
    "    sharex=sharex,\n",
    "    ci=\"sd\",\n",
    "    # flierprops=dict(markerfacecolor='0.75', markersize=5, linestyle='none'),\n",
    "    # showmeans=True,\n",
    "    # meanprops=dict(markerfacecolor=\"white\", markeredgecolor=\"black\"),\n",
    "    height=7,\n",
    "    aspect=1,\n",
    "    palette=palette,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "aggdict = {\n",
    "    \"n_viable_transitions\": [np.mean, np.std],\n",
    "    \"earnings_delta_closest_switch_sum_mio\": np.mean,\n",
    "    \"viability_threshold\": \"first\",\n",
    "}\n",
    "df_annot = df.groupby([\"job_pool\", \"COUNTRYW\", \"reskilling_mode\"]).agg(aggdict)\n",
    "df_annot.columns = [\"_\".join(col) for col in df_annot.columns]\n",
    "df_annot = df_annot.reindex(order, level=1).reset_index()\n",
    "\n",
    "# annotate vline\n",
    "axes = g.axes.flatten()\n",
    "for i, ax in enumerate(axes):\n",
    "    ax.grid(linestyle=\":\", axis=\"x\")\n",
    "    ax.axvline(1, linestyle=\"--\", color=\"lightgrey\", zorder=0)\n",
    "    ax.set_xlabel(\"Job transition options (-)\")  # \"Annual earnings changes (M€, 2019)\"\n",
    "\n",
    "    # annotate numbers (one container per hue level)\n",
    "    for container in ax.containers:\n",
    "        df_hue = df_annot.loc[\n",
    "            (df_annot[hue] == container.get_label())\n",
    "            & (df_annot[\"job_pool\"] == col_order[i])\n",
    "        ]\n",
    "        labels = (\n",
    "            df_hue.loc[:, \"n_viable_transitions_mean\"].round(1).astype(str)\n",

    "            + df_hue.loc[:, \"n_viable_transitions_std\"].round(1).astype(str)\n",
    "        )\n",
    "        ax.bar_label(container, labels=labels, fontsize=8, label_type=\"center\")\n",
    "\n",
    "        # annotate mean\n",
    "        x = df_hue[\"n_viable_transitions_mean\"].mean()\n",
    "        c = container[-1].get_facecolor()\n",
    "        ax.axvline(x, linestyle=\"--\", color=c, label=r\"$\\mu$\")  # , zorder=0)\n",
    "\n",
    "        ax.text(\n",
    "            x,\n",
    "            0,\n",
    "            \"$\\mu = {:.1f}$\".format(x),\n",
    "            rotation=90,\n",
    "            va=\"bottom\",\n",
    "            ha=\"center\",\n",
    "            fontsize=8,\n",
    "        )\n",
    "\n",
    "# save\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",

    "    ),\n",
